title: Phrasing in practice
goal: Worked examples, savings, and how to try the grammar today.

blocks.x: Steno order: left bank (starter), vowels and star, right bank. With no vowels or star, `-` marks the start of the right bank, as in {{I am}} [[SWR-B]].

*there* takes *be*, *have been* and the modals only, not the other verbs, and no bare *do*: [[=there is|STHR-B]], [[=there was|STHREB]], [[=there would be|STHROEB]], [[=there must have been|STHRAUFB]].
What it takes from today's dictionary

Today 37 of the 3,758 grammar strokes are held by other entries: 19 merged two-word phrases and 18 short forms, extras and backups of rare words. The generator will place the grammar first; displaced words take their next outline. In the prototype no word is left without an outline.

Measured by `tools/phrasing_prototype.py` over today's dictionary, today's merged phrases first. By tier: starter plus auxiliary alone saves 0.6%; adding *be*, *have*, *have been*, 1.4%; the 20 verbs, 2.1%. Five verbs (*say*, *see*, *know*, *think*, *go*) are 46% of the verbs' share. The novels are third-person past narration; everyday first- and second-person present typing has more of these pairs per word, so this undercounts.

cargo run --release -- build
python3 tools/phrasing_prototype.py         # writes out/grammar-trial/
cp out/grammar-trial/02-lyk-*.json ~/.config/keymux/steno/lyk/

The trial folder is the `02-lyk-*` set minus the displaced entries, plus the grammar as `02-lyk-grammar.json`. `lyk deploy` restores the normal dictionary (it removes any `02-lyk-` file it did not write).

items: Questions: *do you*, *are you*, *can I* (the starter after the auxiliary).
